- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment drops to 0.00 or below, model often fails to correct downward; apply a downward bias of 2–5% if sentiment remains negative for 3+ days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.  
- Model underestimates mean reversion in downward trends; if 3+ consecutive days show falling prices, add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast to counteract mean reversion.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter: average last 5 forecast values before adjusting for sentiment-driven outliers.
